# error404.ai — the user-facing app that is also the pitch

## Context

Hackathon "Temporal AI" (EHL Zurich). Submission 2026-09-13 10:00 UTC; ~10 h left.
Product: a traveller shares a Deutsche Bahn connection from the DB app (or pastes it, or builds it from → to) into our web app / installable PWA. The app shows the journey on a real 3D globe that zooms from Earth to the route, predicts each train's delay, chains them into **"Probability your plan fails: NN%"**, and gives plain advice ("leave 50 min earlier on ICE 1001"). Users interact with it directly. **The team presents by using the app live on a projector** — the same screens, the same flow, no separate slide mode. The only presenting aids are a large-type "stage" layout and keyboard shortcuts to advance the real flow.

State of the repo: `app/frontend` is an empty placeholder; `app/backend` only has Nebius training routes; the ML model (`app/agents`) has no serving path. The contract is DRAFT (code against it, mock what is missing). `owners.md` is blank → claim frontend + the four backend product features for Akshat.

Decisions taken with the user:
- **MapLibre GL JS `projection: 'globe'`**, free Carto dark raster tiles (no key); SW caches tiles seen in rehearsal.
- **Higgsfield: assets only, ≤ 20 credits** (icons, one backdrop). Website builder rejected (video-scrub product, ~100 credits/film, no PWA/share-target).
- Real DB Navigator share sample (English, int.bahn.de):
  ```
  Nürnberg Hbf → München Hbf
  Sun 13.09.2026
  RB16 (59143)
  To München Hbf
  From 04:34 Nürnberg Hbf, Platform 5 C-F
  To 07:25 München Hbf, Platform 21
  View journey: https://int.bahn.de/en/buchung/start?vbid=e6285f4d-...
  ```
- Seed route: user wants it picked from the Nebius bucket data. Bucket `error404-db-route` (606 objects, ~579 MB, created tonight) exists but `.env` has no S3 keys, so I could not list it. **Assumption: Berlin Hbf → Frankfurt(Main) Hbf → Basel SBB → Zürich HB** as default; it lives in one fixture per layer (5-minute swap). The model is trained on all stations, so any route works. Ask user to run `! bash app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/nebius/sync_bucket.sh ls` once S3 keys are in `.env`, or to name the route.

## What the user sees (single-page app, `app/frontend`)

Full-bleed dark globe, glass panel overlay (right rail ≥ 1024 px, bottom sheet on phone). One flow, four screens, all interactive:

1. **Start** — globe slowly spinning over Europe. Panel: "Will my plan hold?" with three ways in: *paste* what the DB app shared (textarea), *build* a journey (from → to station search over `stations.json`, date/time, legs auto-suggested from a fixture or the DB Timetables API if creds exist), or *try the demo journey*. Web-share-target (`/share?text=`) lands here with the text pre-filled and auto-runs.
2. **Journey** — globe flies from space to the route; legs draw one by one with station pins; cards per leg (train, from → to, planned times, transfer pill). Tap a leg card ⇄ camera flies to that leg; tap a pin ⇄ card highlights. Drag/zoom the globe freely.
3. **Forecast** — legs recolour by risk (green/amber/red); each card gains "+8 min · likely 1–27"; a chain strip shows transfer nodes shrinking; the breaking transfer gets a fly-to; headline counts up to **NN%**. "Why?" disclosure on every number shows `reasoning` + `sources` + confidence (never presented as calibrated). A **buffer slider** ("if I had +N min at Frankfurt…") re-chains live in the browser using the ported connection math — the interactive "what-if".
4. **Advice** — verdict badge + weather-style advice; "Show alternative" draws the earlier connection dashed and fits both; "Compare" toggles between them; "Share result" (Web Share API) and "Install app" prompt.
   Plus two small in-app panels reachable from a footer/menu, used during the pitch: **Proof** (our model vs GPT/Opus baseline, inline SVG bars from `public/proof.json`, PNG fallback) and **About** (the umbrella line, install icon).

**Stage mode** (`?stage=1` or key `S`): same app, bigger type (`html[data-stage]`), progress dots, and keys → / ← that advance the real flow (start → demo journey → forecast → advice → proof → about) and Esc to leave. `F` fullscreen, `M` toggles motion. Works with the backend down (bundled seed fixtures).

## Frontend build

Mirror config from `team-setup/board/web/` (`package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `components.json`, `index.html`, `src/index.css`, `src/lib/utils.ts`, `src/components/ui/{button,card}.tsx`, importing `cn` from `@/lib/utils`). Never edit the board.

Deps (pinned): react/react-dom 19.2.8, vite 8.2.2, @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.1, tailwindcss + @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3, typescript 7.0.2, radix-ui 1.6.7, lucide-react 1.41.0, cva/clsx/tailwind-merge/tw-animate-css, **maplibre-gl 6.9.0**, **motion 13.2.0**, **vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0** + workbox-build/window 7.4.1.

`vite.config.ts`: `@` alias; dev proxy `/api → 127.0.0.1:8000`; `VitePWA` with manifest (name, short_name "error404", standalone, `#07070c`, icons 192/512/maskable, `share_target: { action: '/share', method: 'GET', params: { title, text, url } }`) and workbox (`navigateFallback`, 4 MB cache limit, Carto tiles CacheFirst 3000 entries, `/api/seed/demo` NetworkFirst).

`src/` layout (feature folders per `app/frontend/README.md`):
- `lib/contract.ts` (types verbatim + `Station.lat?/lon?`), `lib/api.ts` (fetch + 8 s timeout), `lib/store.tsx` (context + reducer, pattern from `team-setup/board/web/src/lib/workspace.tsx`; screen, journey, prediction, recommendation, selectedLeg, bufferOverride, showAlt, offline, stage), `lib/chain.ts` (JS port of `connection.py` shared with backend copy, used by the slider), `lib/stations.json` + `stations.ts` (~45 DE/CH/AT hubs, eva/lat/lon/aliases, name normalisation), `lib/geo.ts`, `lib/motion.ts`.
- `features/pwa-shell/` AppShell, OfflineBanner, InstallButton, `useRoute` (`/`, `/share`), `useShareTarget`, `useStageKeys`.
- `features/globe-map/` GlobeMap/useMap (globe, raster, idle spin, StrictMode-safe cleanup), useRouteLayers (per-leg line + glow layers, animated `line-gradient` draw, pins, dashed alt, hover/click → store), camera.ts (`fitRoute` with panel padding, `flyToLeg`, `flyToStation`, `home`).
- `features/share-parser/` StartPanel (paste / build / demo tabs), JourneyBuilder (station combobox, add leg), SharePage, JourneyCards/LegCard.
- `features/delay-prediction/` ForecastPanel, LegDelayRow, ChainStrip, FailHeadline (count-up), BufferSlider, WhyDisclosure.
- `features/recommendation/` AdvicePanel, AlternativeCompare, ShareResult.
- `features/proof/` ProofPanel (SVG bars from `public/proof.json`, fallback png), AboutPanel.
- `public/seed/{journey,prediction,recommendation}.json`, `public/proof.json`, icons.
- `index.css`: dark tokens, glass cards, risk colours, `--db-red` wordmark only, reduced-motion, stage scale, safe-area.

Assets via Higgsfield (`higgsfield generate cost` first; ≤ 20 credits): app mark via `recraft_v4_1`, maskable variant, one dark backdrop via `gpt_image_2_5`; `sips` to resize. Fallback: hand SVG.

## Backend (just enough for the app; zero npm deps)

Copy the pattern in `app/backend/src/features/training-jobs/routes/training-jobs.js` (service factory + `registerRoutes`; errors via `Object.assign(new Error(), {status})`); tests via `Router` like `training-jobs.test.js`.

- `server.js`: health adds `ok: true`; `CORS_ORIGIN` + `OPTIONS` 204 before routing; order route → `/api` 404 → static file → SPA index → 404. Register four features, inject predict into recommendation.
- `features/pwa-shell/`: `static.js` (serve `app/frontend/dist`: traversal guard, MIME incl. `.webmanifest`, no-cache for index/sw/manifest, immutable `/assets`, HEAD, streams, SPA fallback); `GET /api/seed/demo` from `fixtures/seed-journey.json` (lat/lon on stations).
- `features/share-parser/`: `grammar.js` tokenizer + state machine built on the real sample (header `A → B`, weekday+date, `RB16 (59143)` → `RB 16`, `To <dest>` direction line, `From HH:MM Station, Platform…` = dep, `To HH:MM Station, Platform…` = arr, `View journey: URL` with vbid; German `Ab/An/Gleis/Nach`; repeated blocks = legs; transfer = next dep − prev arr; `Verbindung N`/`Connection N` boundaries → first complete). `stations.js` normalisation + `fixtures/stations.json` + optional DB Timetables `station/{pattern}` lookup. `vbid.js` behind `BAHN_VBID_RESOLVER=1`, else 422 with hint. Fixtures: real sample, German variant, 3-leg seed text, two-connections, URL-only.
- `features/delay-prediction/`: `connection.js` port of `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/connection.py` (+ ported tests), `backends/mock.js` deterministic geometric pmf by class × hour × duration (`modelId 'mock-prior-v1'`, confidence low), `backends/http.js` for `PREDICT_URL` with fallback; `chain(journey, forecasts)` pure; `Explained` strings in `predict.py` wording.
- `features/recommendation/`: good < 0.15; buffer search 5..30 at weakest transfer via `chain` → add-buffer; else take-alternative from `fixtures/alternatives.json` (50 min earlier, +25 min transfers) or synthesized. Weather-voice advice.
- `.env.example` (+ commented `CORS_ORIGIN`, `STATIC_DIR`, `PREDICT_URL`, `PREDICT_BACKEND`, `PREDICT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `MIN_TRANSFER_MINUTES`, `BAHN_VBID_RESOLVER`), feature READMEs, backend README.

## Coordination edits
`owners.md` (Akshat: `app/frontend`, backend `pwa-shell`/`share-parser`/`delay-prediction`/`recommendation`); `decisions.md` append: stack + globe + Higgsfield-assets-only; **proposed** additive `Station.lat/lon` (needs sign-off); seed route default pending bucket check. `tasks.json`: PWA, share-parser, core prediction, recommendation → building.

| 08:30–10:00 | Two live rehearsals, backup screen recording, fixes, READMEs, owners/decisions |

=== anchors.py
"""Choose the travel dates each entity is trained on.

An anchor is a **travel date**, not a cursor into a file. The sample is "on the
day before this anchor, predict how late this train will be at this stop over
the next ``HORIZON_DAYS``", so the anchor splits time into a context that ends
at the anchor and a horizon that starts the day after. Nothing here knows what
a profile is: ``profiles.HORIZON_DAYS``, ``ANCHOR_STRIDE_DAYS`` and
``RECENCY_HALF_LIFE_DAYS`` are read from the frozen contract and the same
anchors are handed to S, M, L and XM. If the anchors differed the bake-off
would not be a controlled comparison.

**How many anchors per entity, and why five.**

Repeated anchors on the same entity are not independent samples -- the same
platform, the same junction, the same timetable. Under the usual
exchangeable-within-cluster model with intra-entity correlation rho, M
observations of one entity carry ``M / (1 + (M-1) rho)`` effective samples, so
the M-th anchor is worth roughly ``1 / (1 + (M-1) rho)^2`` of a fresh entity.
With the measured pair-level rho ~ 0.20:

    M =  1   1.00 effective   (20% of the asymptote)
    M =  5   2.78 effective   (56%)
    M = 10   3.57 effective   (71%)
    M = 20   4.17 effective   (83%)
    M -> inf 5.00 effective   -- the asymptote is 1/rho, whatever M you pick

That asymptote is the whole argument. Beyond 1/rho = 5 effective samples per
entity there is nothing left to buy, so the question is only how cheaply to get
most of it. M=5 captures 56% at a quarter of the anchors M=20 needs, and the
budget freed goes into *more entities*, where the returns are still linear.

**Why the window start is staggered per entity.**

Two things are wanted at once and they pull opposite ways. Per entity the
anchors should sit close together, because a short per-entity span means the
five anchors describe one timetable regime and the design effect stays near the
1.8 the arithmetic above assumes. Across the corpus the anchors should cover
every week available, or the model only ever sees one season. Staggering
resolves it: each entity gets a deterministic offset from a hash of its id, so
its own span stays ``(M-1) * ANCHOR_GAP_DAYS`` while the *union* over thousands
of entities tiles the whole archive. The offset is a hash rather than a draw
because the corpus has to be reproducible from the entity list alone.

**Why the gap is 35 and not 30.**

30 days apart is the requirement; 35 is 30 rounded up onto the
``ANCHOR_STRIDE_DAYS`` = 7 grid. Staying on the grid means every anchor of an
entity falls on the same weekday, so the five horizons are the same seven
weekdays and the five samples differ by date rather than by which days of the
week they happen to contain. The weekday itself is then set per entity by

input.content:
# error404.ai — interactive web app + PWA with a globe route view

## Context

We are building the user-facing product: a web app (installable PWA) where a traveller drops in a Deutsche Bahn connection and sees, on a real 3D globe that zooms from Earth to the route, how late each train will be, the chained **"Probability your plan fails: NN%"**, and plain advice. Users interact with it directly, and the team will also present by using the same app live on a big screen, so it needs a large-type stage layout and keyboard shortcuts that advance the real flow. No separate slide mode.

Repo state after `git pull` (main is current): `app/frontend` is an empty placeholder, `app/backend` only has Nebius training routes, the ML model has no serving path. The API contract (`team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md`) defines the types and the four endpoints below; we code against it and mock what is missing.

Decisions already made with the user:
- **Map**: MapLibre GL JS with `projection: 'globe'`, free Carto dark raster tiles (no API key), service worker caches tiles seen during rehearsal.
- **Higgsfield**: assets only, ≤ 20 credits (app icon, maskable icon, one dark backdrop). The Higgsfield website builder is not used (video-scrub product, ~100 credits per film, no PWA or share-target support).
- **Share text format** (real DB Navigator sample from the user, English, int.bahn.de):
  ```
  Nürnberg Hbf → München Hbf
  Sun 13.09.2026
  RB16 (59143)
  To München Hbf
  From 04:34 Nürnberg Hbf, Platform 5 C-F
  To 07:25 München Hbf, Platform 21
  View journey: https://int.bahn.de/en/buchung/start?vbid=e6285f4d-...
  ```
- **Route data**: the new branch `origin/feat/db-route-multiscale` (matching the `error404-db-route` bucket on Nebius) builds training data for six commuter regions, Munich, Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, using S-Bahn and regional trains only. The seed journey therefore stays regional and inside a covered region: **leg 1 = the user's own sample (RB 16, Nürnberg Hbf 04:34 → München Hbf 07:25), leg 2 = S 8 München Hbf 07:41 → München Flughafen Terminal 08:22, transfer 16 min.** It lives in one fixture per layer so it can be swapped in minutes. The S3 keys are not in `.env`, so the bucket objects themselves were not listed.

## Architecture

```
DB app share ──GET /share?text=…──▶  PWA  (Vite + React 19, app/frontend/dist)
                                        │ same origin (service worker + share target require it)
                                        ▼
                    Node backend :8000 (zero npm deps) serves dist and /api
  POST /api/journeys/parse   share-parser      grammar for the share text + stations table
  POST /api/predict          delay-prediction  mock prior now, PREDICT_URL → Python model later;
                                               JS port of connection.py chains the legs
  POST /api/recommend        recommendation    rules + alternative connection
  GET  /api/seed/demo        pwa-shell         seed journey (also bundled in the frontend for offline)
Phone over HTTPS: cloudflared quick tunnel → localhost:8000
```

## The app (what users see)

Full-bleed dark globe; a glass panel overlays it (right rail ≥ 1024 px, bottom sheet on phones). One flow, four screens, all interactive:

1. **Start** — globe slowly turning over Europe. Panel "Will my plan hold?" with three ways in: *Paste* what the DB app shared, *Build* a journey (from → to station search, time, add legs), *Try the demo journey*. Arriving via the share target pre-fills the text and runs automatically.
2. **Journey** — camera flies from space down to the route; legs draw one by one with station pins; one card per leg (train, from → to, planned times, transfer pill). Tap a card → camera flies to that leg; tap a pin → card highlights. Globe stays freely draggable and zoomable.
3. **Forecast** — legs recolour by risk (green / amber / red); cards show "+8 min · likely 1–27"; a chain strip shows each transfer shrinking; the breaking transfer gets a fly-to; the headline counts up to NN%. Every number has a "Why?" disclosure with reasoning, sources and confidence. A **buffer slider** ("if I had +N min at München Hbf…") re-chains live in the browser.
4. **Advice** — verdict badge and weather-style advice; "Show alternative" draws the earlier connection dashed and fits both; "Compare" toggles; "Share result" (Web Share API); "Install app".
   Footer menu: **Proof** (our model vs GPT/Claude baseline, inline SVG bars from `public/proof.json`, PNG fallback) and **About** (the "take an umbrella" line).

**Stage mode** (`?stage=1` or key `S`): same screens, bigger type via `html[data-stage]`, progress dots; → / ← advance the real flow (start → demo journey → forecast → advice → proof → about), Esc exits, `F` fullscreen, `M` toggles motion. Works with the backend down thanks to bundled seed fixtures.

## Frontend build (`app/frontend`)

Copy config from the working setup in `team-setup/board/web/` (`package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `components.json`, `index.html`, `src/index.css`, `src/lib/utils.ts`, `src/components/ui/{button,card}.tsx`; import `cn` from `@/lib/utils`). Do not edit the board itself.

Dependencies (pinned): react/react-dom 19.2.8, vite 8.2.2, @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.1, tailwindcss + @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3, typescript 7.0.2, radix-ui 1.6.7, lucide-react 1.41.0, class-variance-authority, clsx, tailwind-merge, tw-animate-css, **maplibre-gl 6.9.0**, **motion 13.2.0**, **vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0** (+ workbox-build / workbox-window 7.4.1).

`vite.config.ts`: `@` alias; dev proxy `/api → http://127.0.0.1:8000`; `VitePWA` with manifest (name, short_name "error404", `display: standalone`, colours `#07070c`, icons 192 / 512 / maskable, `share_target: { action: '/share', method: 'GET', params: { title, text, url } }`) and workbox (`navigateFallback: /index.html`, 4 MB precache limit for the MapLibre chunk, Carto tiles CacheFirst up to 3000 entries, `/api/seed/demo` NetworkFirst).

`src/` (one folder per feature, as `app/frontend/README.md` asks):
- `lib/contract.ts` (types from the contract + optional `Station.lat/lon`), `lib/api.ts` (fetch with 8 s timeout: parseJourney, predict, recommend, seedDemo, health), `lib/store.tsx` (context + `useReducer`, same pattern as `team-setup/board/web/src/lib/workspace.tsx`: screen, journey, prediction, recommendation, selectedLeg, bufferOverride, showAlt, offline, stage; `runFromText`, `runFromSeed` with fallback to `public/seed/*.json`), `lib/chain.ts` (JS port of `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/connection.py` for the slider), `lib/stations.json` + `stations.ts` (~45 DE/CH/AT hubs plus Munich S-Bahn stops: name, evaNumber, lat, lon, aliases; normalisation of umlauts, "Hbf", parentheses), `lib/geo.ts` (leg lines, bounds, risk colour: < 0.15 green, < 0.4 amber, else red), `lib/motion.ts` (reduced-motion and `?motion=0`).
- `features/pwa-shell/`: AppShell, OfflineBanner, InstallButton (`beforeinstallprompt`), `hooks/useRoute.ts` (`/` and `/share`, no router lib), `hooks/useShareTarget.ts`, `hooks/useStageKeys.ts`.
- `features/globe-map/`: GlobeMap + `useMap` (globe projection, dark background, raster source, idle spin, StrictMode-safe `map.remove()`), `useRouteLayers` (GeoJSON per journey, per-leg line + glow layers, animated draw via `line-gradient` on `line-progress` ~700 ms per leg, station circles, dashed alternative, click/hover → store), `camera.ts` (`fitRoute` with panel padding, `flyToLeg`, `flyToStation` zoom 9.5 pitch 45, `home`).
- `features/share-parser/`: StartPanel (paste / build / demo), JourneyBuilder (station combobox, add leg), SharePage, JourneyCards, LegCard.
- `features/delay-prediction/`: ForecastPanel, LegDelayRow, ChainStrip, FailHeadline (count-up with `motion`), BufferSlider, WhyDisclosure.
- `features/recommendation/`: AdvicePanel, AlternativeCompare, ShareResult.
- `features/proof/`: ProofPanel (SVG bars), AboutPanel.
- `public/seed/{journey,prediction,recommendation}.json`, `public/proof.json`, `public/icons/*`.

No separate slide mode.

Repo state after `git pull` (main is current): `app/frontend` is an empty placeholder, `app/backend` only has Nebius training routes, the ML model has no serving path. The API contract (`team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md`) defines the types and the four endpoints below; we code against it and mock what is missing.

Decisions already made with the user:
- **Map**: MapLibre GL JS with `projection: 'globe'`, free Carto dark raster tiles (no API key), service worker caches tiles seen during rehearsal.

  ```
  Nürnberg Hbf → München Hbf
  Sun 13.09.2026
  RB16 (59143)
  To München Hbf
  From 04:34 Nürnberg Hbf, Platform 5 C-F
  To 07:25 München Hbf, Platform 21
  View journey: https://int.bahn.de/en/buchung/start?vbid=e6285f4d-...
  ```
- **Route data**: the new branch `origin/feat/db-route-multiscale` (matching the `error404-db-route` bucket on Nebius) builds training data for six commuter regions, Munich, Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, using S-Bahn and regional trains only. The seed journey therefore stays regional and inside a covered region: **leg 1 = the user's own sample (RB 16, Nürnberg Hbf 04:34 → München Hbf 07:25), leg 2 = S 8 München Hbf 07:41 → München Flughafen Terminal 08:22, transfer 16 min.** It lives in one fixture per layer so it can be swapped in minutes. DB app share ──GET /share?text=…──▶  PWA  (Vite + React 19, app/frontend/dist)

  POST /api/predict          delay-prediction  mock prior now, PREDICT_URL → Python model later;
                                               JS port of connection.py chains the legs
  POST /api/recommend        recommendation    rules + alternative connection
  GET  /api/seed/demo        pwa-shell         seed journey (also bundled in the frontend for offline)
Phone over HTTPS: cloudflared quick tunnel → localhost:8000
```

## The app (what users see)

Full-bleed dark globe; a glass panel overlays it (right rail ≥ 1024 px, bottom sheet on phones). One flow, four screens, all interactive:

1. **Start** — globe slowly turning over Europe. Panel "Will my plan hold?" with three ways in: *Paste* what the DB app shared, *Build* a journey (from → to station search, time, add legs), *Try the demo journey*. Arriving via the share target pre-fills the text and runs automatically.
2. **Journey** — camera flies from space down to the route; legs draw one by one with station pins; one card per leg (train, from → to, planned times, transfer pill). Tap a card → camera flies to that leg; tap a pin → card highlights. Globe stays freely draggable and zoomable.

# error404.ai — interactive web app + PWA with a globe route view

## Context

We are building the user-facing product: a web app (installable PWA) where a traveller drops in a Deutsche Bahn connection and sees, on a real 3D globe that zooms from Earth to the route, how late each train will be, the chained **"Probability your plan fails: NN%"**, and plain advice. Users interact with it directly, and the team will also present by using the same app live on a big screen, so it needs a large-type stage layout and keyboard shortcuts that advance the real flow. No separate slide mode.

Repo state after `git pull` (main is current): `app/frontend` is an empty placeholder, `app/backend` only has Nebius training routes, the ML model has no serving path. The API contract (`team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md`) defines the types and the four endpoints below; we code against it and mock what is missing.

Decisions already made with the user:
- **Map**: MapLibre GL JS with `projection: 'globe'`, free Carto dark raster tiles (no API key), service worker caches tiles seen during rehearsal.
- **Higgsfield**: assets only, ≤ 20 credits (app icon, maskable icon, one dark backdrop). The Higgsfield website builder is not used (video-scrub product, ~100 credits per film, no PWA or share-target support).
- **Share text format** (real DB Navigator sample from the user, English, int.bahn.de):
  ```
  Nürnberg Hbf → München Hbf
  Sun 13.09.2026
  RB16 (59143)
  To München Hbf
  From 04:34 Nürnberg Hbf, Platform 5 C-F
  To 07:25 München Hbf, Platform 21
  View journey: https://int.bahn.de/en/buchung/start?vbid=e6285f4d-...
  ```
- **Route data**: the new branch `origin/feat/db-route-multiscale` (matching the `error404-db-route` bucket on Nebius) builds training data for six commuter regions, Munich, Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, using S-Bahn and regional trains only. The seed journey therefore stays regional and inside a covered region: **leg 1 = the user's own sample (RB 16, Nürnberg Hbf 04:34 → München Hbf 07:25), leg 2 = S 8 München Hbf 07:41 → München Flughafen Terminal 08:22, transfer 16 min.** It lives in one fixture per layer so it can be swapped in minutes. The S3 keys are not in `.env`, so the bucket objects themselves were not listed.

```
DB app share ──GET /share?text=…──▶  PWA  (Vite + React 19, app/frontend/dist)

                    Node backend :8000 (zero npm deps) serves dist and /api

  POST /api/predict          delay-prediction  mock prior now, PREDICT_URL → Python model later;
                                               JS port of connection.py chains the legs
  POST /api/recommend        recommendation    rules + alternative connection
  GET  /api/seed/demo        pwa-shell         seed journey (also bundled in the frontend for offline)
Phone over HTTPS: cloudflared quick tunnel → localhost:8000
```

## The app (what users see)

Full-bleed dark globe; a glass panel overlays it (right rail ≥ 1024 px, bottom sheet on phones). One flow, four screens, all interactive:

1. **Start** — globe slowly turning over Europe. Panel "Will my plan hold?" with three ways in: *Paste* what the DB app shared, *Build* a journey (from → to station search, time, add legs), *Try the demo journey*. Arriving via the share target pre-fills the text and runs automatically.
2. **Journey** — camera flies from space down to the route; legs draw one by one with station pins; one card per leg (train, from → to, planned times, transfer pill). Tap a card → camera flies to that leg; tap a pin → card highlights. Globe stays freely draggable and zoomable.
3. **Forecast** — legs recolour by risk (green / amber / red); cards show "+8 min · likely 1–27"; a chain strip shows each transfer shrinking; the breaking transfer gets a fly-to; the headline counts up to NN%. Every number has a "Why?" disclosure with reasoning, sources and confidence. A **buffer slider** ("if I had +N min at München Hbf…") re-chains live in the browser.
4. **Advice** — verdict badge and weather-style advice; "Show alternative" draws the earlier connection dashed and fits both; "Compare" toggles; "Share result" (Web Share API); "Install app".
   Footer menu: **Proof** (our model vs GPT/Claude baseline, inline SVG bars from `public/proof.json`, PNG fallback) and **About** (the "take an umbrella" line).

**Stage mode** (`?stage=1` or key `S`): same screens, bigger type via `html[data-stage]`, progress dots; → / ← advance the real flow (start → demo journey → forecast → advice → proof → about), Esc exits, `F` fullscreen, `M` toggles motion. # error404.ai — PWA with 3D globe, DB-app share target, forecast, re-route and causes

## Context

We are building the user-facing product: an installable PWA where a traveller either **drops / pastes a DB connection** or **presses Share in the DB app, sees our app in the share sheet, taps it, and lands in our app** with the journey loaded. The app shows the route on a real 3D globe that zooms from Earth to the trains, the **probability each train is delayed and the plan fails**, **recommendations** (how early to leave home, what to do when a connection is missed, best re-route), and **causes of delay** with the evidence and the limitations. The team also presents by using this same app live on a big screen (large-type stage layout + keys that advance the real flow). Everything the user or audience sees is on the frontend; the backend only serves data.

Repo state (after `git pull`, main current): `app/frontend` is an empty placeholder, `app/backend` only has Nebius training routes, the model has no serving path. We code against the draft contract (`team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md`) and mock what is missing, with additive fields only.

Decisions already made with the user:
- **Map**: MapLibre GL JS `projection: 'globe'`, free Carto dark raster tiles (no key); service worker caches tiles seen in rehearsal.
- **Higgsfield**: assets only, ≤ 20 credits (icon, maskable icon, one backdrop). Website builder not used.
- **Share text** (real DB Navigator sample from the user, English, int.bahn.de):
  ```
  Nürnberg Hbf → München Hbf
  Sun 13.09.2026
  RB16 (59143)
  To München Hbf
  From 04:34 Nürnberg Hbf, Platform 5 C-F
  To 07:25 München Hbf, Platform 21
  View journey: https://int.bahn.de/en/buchung/start?vbid=e6285f4d-...
  ```
- **Data / route**: branch `origin/feat/db-route-multiscale` (matches the `error404-db-route` bucket) sources `piebro/deutsche-bahn-data` (CC BY 4.0, DB Timetables/IRIS data) for six commuter regions, Munich, Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, with S-Bahn and regional trains, and attributes causes from IRIS codes into families **works, weather, technical, knock_on, staff, external**, with an explicit "unattributed" floor (only ~30 % of stops carry a cause). Seed journey stays regional inside a covered region: **leg 1 = the user's sample (RB 16, Nürnberg Hbf 04:34 → München Hbf 07:25), leg 2 = S 8 München Hbf 07:41 → München Flughafen Terminal 08:22, 16 min transfer.** One fixture per layer, swappable in minutes. (S3 keys are not in `.env`, so the bucket objects were not listed.)

### Share-sheet facts the demo depends on
- The app appears in the Android share sheet only when the PWA is **installed** from an **HTTPS** origin in Chrome and its manifest declares `share_target`. So the demo phone must install it via the tunnel URL first. iOS Safari does not support `share_target` (paste/drop path covers iPhone).
- The DB app shares plain text (+ URL), so `share_target` uses `method: GET`, `action: /share`, params `title/text/url`. Our `/share` route reads the query, strips it from the URL, and runs parse → predict → recommend automatically.
- Same origin is required for the manifest, service worker and share target, so the backend serves the built frontend.

## Architecture

```
DB app Share ─▶ share sheet ─▶ error404 (installed PWA) ─▶ GET /share?text=…
Paste / drop text or .txt ─▶ Start screen                         │
                                                                   ▼
                    PWA (Vite + React 19, app/frontend/dist) ── same origin ──▶ Node backend :8000 (zero deps)
  POST /api/journeys/parse   share-parser       grammar for share text + stations table
  POST /api/predict          delay-prediction   mock prior now / PREDICT_URL → Python later; JS port of connection.py
  POST /api/recommend        recommendation     leave-home time, buffer, alternative
  POST /api/reroute          recommendation     next connections after a missed transfer (fixture, live Timetables if creds)
  GET  /api/causes           causes             cause-family shares per station / region (fixture from the pipeline output)
  GET  /api/seed/demo        pwa-shell          seed journey (also bundled in the frontend for offline)
Phone: cloudflared quick tunnel → https://…trycloudflare.com → localhost:8000
```

## The app, screen by screen (all frontend)

Full-bleed dark globe; a glass panel overlays it (right rail ≥ 1024 px, bottom sheet on phones). Bottom tab bar: **Plan · Forecast · Advice · Causes · Evidence**.

1. **Start / Plan** — globe turning over Europe. "Will my plan hold?" with: *Paste or drop* (textarea that also accepts drag-and-drop of text or a `.txt`), *Build* (from → to station search, time, add legs), *Demo journey*. A one-line hint "or press Share in the DB app and pick error404". Arriving from the share sheet skips this screen.
2. **Journey** — camera flies from space to the route; legs draw one by one with pins; one card per leg (train, from → to, planned times, transfer pill). Tap card ⇄ fly to leg; tap pin ⇄ highlight card. Globe stays draggable.
3. **Forecast** (visual 1) — per leg: **delay-probability bar chart** (P(delay ≤ 5), 5–15, 15–30, > 30, cancelled) from the returned distribution, "+8 min · likely 1–27", risk colour on the map leg; chain strip with transfers shrinking; fly-to on the breaking transfer; headline counts up to **"Probability your plan fails: NN%"**. Every number has "Why?" (reasoning, sources, confidence). **Buffer slider** re-chains live in the browser.
4. **Advice** (visuals 2 + 3) — verdict + weather-style advice. **"Leave home by HH:MM"**: user sets minutes from door to first station and an acceptable risk; the app picks the earliest departure (alternatives from the backend) that meets it and shows the time. **"I missed my connection"** per transfer → re-route list: next trains from that station with their own fail probability, best one highlighted and drawn dashed on the map; "Compare" toggles original vs re-route.
5. **Causes** (visual 4) — for the selected station or leg: stacked bar of cause-family shares (works, weather, technical, knock-on, staff, external, unattributed), a 7-day sparkline of station delay, and the IRIS text of the top cause. Data from `/api/causes` with a bundled fixture fallback; the source line states the dataset and the ~30 % attribution rate.
6. **Evidence** — three cards: *Data* (where it comes from: piebro/deutsche-bahn-data over DB IRIS, six regions, months covered, the DB Timetables API for live station lookup), *Results* (our model vs GPT/Claude baseline: one SVG bar chart from `public/proof.json` with the metric name, split, n; PNG fallback), *Limitations* (only 30 % of delays carry a cause; transfers treated as independent; regional trains in six regions, long-distance and other regions are out of scope; confidence is advisory, not calibrated; live prediction currently uses a prior when the model server is offline, shown as a badge). This card set is what the audience sees when the presenter explains evidence and limits.

**Stage mode** (`?stage=1` or key `S`): same screens, bigger type, progress dots; → / ← walk: Plan → share arrives → Journey → Forecast → Advice → re-route → Causes → Evidence. Esc exits, `F` fullscreen, `M` toggles motion. Works with the backend down (bundled fixtures) and shows a small "offline · seed" pill when it does.

## Frontend build (`app/frontend`)

Copy config from `team-setup/board/web/` (`package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `components.json`, `index.html`, `src/index.css`, `src/lib/utils.ts`, `src/components/ui/{button,card}.tsx`; import `cn` from `@/lib/utils`). Do not edit the board.

Dependencies (pinned): react/react-dom 19.2.8, vite 8.2.2, @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.1, tailwindcss + @tailwindcss/vite 4.3.3, typescript 7.0.2, radix-ui 1.6.7, lucide-react 1.41.0, class-variance-authority, clsx, tailwind-merge, tw-animate-css, **maplibre-gl 6.9.0**, **motion 13.2.0**, **vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0** (+ workbox-build / workbox-window 7.4.1). Charts are plain inline SVG (no chart library).

`vite.config.ts`: `@` alias; dev proxy `/api → http://127.0.0.1:8000`; `VitePWA({ registerType: 'autoUpdate', manifest: { name, short_name: 'error404', display: 'standalone', theme/background '#07070c', icons 192/512/maskable, share_target: { action: '/share', method: 'GET', params: { title: 'title', text: 'text', url: 'url' } } }, workbox: { navigateFallback: '/index.html', maximumFileSizeToCacheInBytes: 4 MB, runtimeCaching: [Carto tiles CacheFirst 3000 entries, /api/seed/demo + /api/causes NetworkFirst] } })`.

`src/` (one folder per feature):
- `lib/contract.ts` (contract types + additive optional fields: `Station.lat/lon`, `LegDelay.distribution`, `Recommendation.leaveHomeBy`), `lib/api.ts` (fetch + 8 s timeout: parseJourney, predict, recommend, reroute, causes, seedDemo, health), `lib/store.tsx` (context + `useReducer`, pattern from `team-setup/board/web/src/lib/workspace.tsx`: tab, journey, prediction, recommendation, reroute, causes, selectedLeg, bufferOverride, doorToStationMin, acceptableRisk, showAlt, offline, stage; thunks `runFromText`, `runFromSeed` with fixture fallback), `lib/chain.ts` (port of `connection.py` for the slider and leave-home calc), `lib/stations.json` + `stations.ts` (~45 hubs + Munich S-Bahn stops: name, evaNumber, lat, lon, aliases; umlaut/“Hbf”/parentheses normalisation), `lib/geo.ts` (leg lines, bounds, risk colour), `lib/motion.ts`.
- `features/pwa-shell/`: AppShell, TabBar, OfflineBanner, InstallButton, `hooks/useRoute.ts` (`/`, `/share`), `hooks/useShareTarget.ts`, `hooks/useStageKeys.ts`, `hooks/useDropText.ts`.
- `features/globe-map/`: GlobeMap + `useMap` (globe, dark background, raster source, idle spin, StrictMode-safe cleanup), `useRouteLayers` (per-leg line + glow, animated `line-gradient` draw, pins, dashed alternative/re-route, click/hover → store), `camera.ts` (`fitRoute` with panel padding, `flyToLeg`, `flyToStation`, `home`).
- `features/share-parser/`: StartPanel (paste/drop, build, demo), JourneyBuilder, SharePage, JourneyCards, LegCard.
- `features/delay-prediction/`: ForecastPanel, LegDelayRow, DelayBars (SVG), ChainStrip, FailHeadline, BufferSlider, WhyDisclosure.
- `features/recommendation/`: AdvicePanel, LeaveHomeBy, MissedConnection (per transfer), RerouteList, AlternativeCompare, ShareResult.
- `features/causes/`: CausesPanel, CauseStack (SVG stacked bar), DelaySparkline.
- `features/evidence/`: EvidencePanel, DataCard, ResultsChart, LimitationsCard.
- `public/seed/{journey,prediction,recommendation,reroute,causes}.json`, `public/proof.json`, `public/icons/*`.
- `index.css`: dark tokens, glass cards, risk colours, DB red for the wordmark only, reduced-motion, stage type scale, safe-area padding.

Assets via Higgsfield CLI (`higgsfield generate cost` first, cap 20 credits): app mark with `recraft_v4_1`, maskable variant, one dark backdrop with `gpt_image_2_5`; resize with `sips`. Fallback: hand SVG.

## Backend (`app/backend`, zero npm deps)

Pattern from `app/backend/src/features/training-jobs/routes/training-jobs.js` (`createXService(ctx)` + `registerRoutes(router, ctx)`; errors `Object.assign(new Error(msg), { status })`). Tests with `node:test` through `Router`, like `training-jobs.test.js`.

- `src/server.js`: health adds `ok: true`; `CORS_ORIGIN` headers + `OPTIONS` 204 before routing; order route → `/api/*` JSON 404 → static file → SPA `index.html` → 404. Register features; inject predict into recommendation.
- `features/pwa-shell/`: `static.js` (traversal guard, MIME incl. `.webmanifest`, no-cache for `index.html`/`sw.js`/manifest, immutable `/assets/*`, HEAD, streaming, SPA fallback); `GET /api/seed/demo` from `fixtures/seed-journey.json` with lat/lon. Default `STATIC_DIR = app/frontend/dist`.
- `features/share-parser/`: `grammar.js` tokenizer + state machine built on the real sample (header `A → B`, weekday + date, `RB16 (59143)` → `RB 16`, `To <dest>` = direction line, `From HH:MM Station, Platform …` = departure, `To HH:MM Station, Platform …` = arrival, `View journey:` URL with vbid; German `Ab/An/Gleis/Nach`; repeated blocks = legs; transfer = next dep − prev arr; `Connection N` boundaries → first complete). `stations.js` + `fixtures/stations.json` + DB Timetables `station/{pattern}` when creds exist. `vbid.js` behind `BAHN_VBID_RESOLVER=1`, else 422 with hint. Fixtures: real sample, German variant, two-leg Munich, two-connections, URL-only.
- `features/delay-prediction/`: `connection.js` port of `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/connection.py` (+ ported tests); `backends/mock.js` deterministic geometric distribution by class × hour × duration (`modelId 'mock-prior-v1'`, confidence low); `backends/http.js` for `PREDICT_URL` with fallback noted in `sources`; `chain(journey, forecasts) → Prediction` including `distribution: { bins: ['≤5','5–15','15–30','>30','cancelled'], probs }` and p10/p50/p90 per leg.
- `features/recommendation/`: `POST /api/recommend` (good < 0.15; buffer search +5…+30 at the weakest transfer; else alternative from `fixtures/alternatives.json` or synthesised; `leaveHomeBy` from `doorToStationMin` + acceptable risk); `POST /api/reroute` `{ journey, missedLegIndex }` → next 3 connections from that station (fixture `fixtures/reroute.json`; live via DB Timetables `plan/{eva}/{yymmdd}/{hh}` filtered by `ppth` when creds exist), each scored with `chain`.
- `features/causes/`: `GET /api/causes?eva=…` → `{ station, families: { works, weather, technical, knock_on, staff, external, unattributed }, top: [{ code, text, share }], sparkline7d, source }` from `fixtures/causes.json` (numbers to be replaced by the pipeline's output from the `db_route` branch when available; the fixture states it is illustrative until then).
- `.env.example`: commented `CORS_ORIGIN`, `STATIC_DIR`, `PREDICT_URL`, `PREDICT_BACKEND`, `PREDICT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `MIN_TRANSFER_MINUTES`, `BAHN_VBID_RESOLVER`. Feature READMEs; endpoints table in `app/backend/README.md`.

## Order of work (frontend-led; backend stubs in a parallel subagent)

1. Backend stubs for all six endpoints from fixtures, static serving, tests green. Frontend scaffold, store, globe with the seed route drawn, `npm run build` green.
2. Plan screen (paste/drop, build, demo), `/share` route + manifest `share_target`, journey cards ⇄ globe, fly-in, leg draw.
3. Forecast: chain port, delay bars, recolouring, chain strip, headline, buffer slider, why-disclosures. Backend: mock prior + parser on the real sample.
4. Advice: leave-home-by, missed-connection re-route list drawn on the map, compare, share result. Backend: rules + reroute.
5. Causes and Evidence tabs (SVG stacked bar, sparkline, proof chart, data + limitations cards). Stage mode keys and type scale. Service worker + icons.
6. Production build served by the backend; `brew install cloudflared`; `cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:8000`; on Android Chrome install the PWA, open the DB app, Share → error404 → journey screen. Warm tile cache. Responsive pass 375 / 768 / 1024 / 1920.
7. Two full live walk-throughs, backup screen recording, fixes, READMEs.

Cut first if short on time: journey builder (keep paste + demo) → live Timetables reroute (fixture only) → vbid resolver → sparkline → http backend → alternative drawn on the map → `motion` dependency → animated line draw → SVG proof (PNG only). Never cut: share target + `/share`, paste path, seed fixtures, headline, delay bars, re-route list, causes stack, evidence cards, stage keys.

## Verification

- Backend: `cd app/backend && npm test`; `npm run dev`; curl `/api/health` (`ok: true`), `/api/seed/demo`, `/api/predict` with the seed (distribution present), `/api/recommend` (`leaveHomeBy` present), `/api/reroute` with `missedLegIndex: 0`, `/api/causes?eva=8000261`, `/api/journeys/parse` with the real sample (→ one leg `RB 16`) and the two-leg text; 400 on junk; `/api/nope` JSON 404; SPA fallback; manifest MIME; `sw.js` no-cache.
- Frontend: `npm run build` clean; dev: demo journey runs the full chain; backend stopped → offline pill, fixtures render on every tab; `/share?text=<urlencoded sample>` works; drop a `.txt` on the start screen works; slider re-chains; card ⇄ pin; leave-home-by changes with door-to-station minutes; "I missed it" shows re-routes and draws the best one; causes stack sums to 100 %; evidence chart renders from `proof.json`; `?stage=1` keys walk every screen forward and back, with backend up and down, and with `motion=0`; responsive checks.
- Phone: PWA installs over the tunnel; **error404 shows in the DB app's share sheet; tapping it opens the app on the journey screen** with the shared connection parsed.
- `bash team-setup/scripts/smoke.sh` passes with `SMOKE_HEALTH_URL=http://localhost:8000/api/health`.

# error404.ai — PWA with 3D globe, DB-app share target, forecast, re-route and causes

## Context

We are building the user-facing product: an installable PWA where a traveller either **drops / pastes a DB connection** or **presses Share in the DB app, sees our app in the share sheet, taps it, and lands in our app** with the journey loaded. The app shows the route on a real 3D globe that zooms from Earth to the trains, the **probability each train is delayed and the plan fails**, **recommendations** (how early to leave home, what to do when a connection is missed, best re-route), and **causes of delay** with the evidence and the limitations. The team also presents by using this same app live on a big screen (large-type stage layout + keys that advance the real flow). Everything the user or audience sees is on the frontend; the backend only serves data.

Repo state (after `git pull`, main current): `app/frontend` is an empty placeholder, `app/backend` only has Nebius training routes, the model has no serving path. We code against the draft contract (`team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md`) and mock what is missing, with additive fields only.

Decisions already made with the user:
- **Map**: MapLibre GL JS `projection: 'globe'`, free Carto dark raster tiles (no key); service worker caches tiles seen in rehearsal.
- **Higgsfield**: assets only, ≤ 20 credits (icon, maskable icon, one backdrop). Website builder not used.
- **Share text** (real DB Navigator sample from the user, English, int.bahn.de):
  ```
  Nürnberg Hbf → München Hbf
  Sun 13.09.2026
  RB16 (59143)
  To München Hbf
  From 04:34 Nürnberg Hbf, Platform 5 C-F
  To 07:25 München Hbf, Platform 21
  View journey: https://int.bahn.de/en/buchung/start?vbid=e6285f4d-...
  ```
- **Data / route**: branch `origin/feat/db-route-multiscale` (matches the `error404-db-route` bucket) sources `piebro/deutsche-bahn-data` (CC BY 4.0, DB Timetables/IRIS data) for six commuter regions, Munich, Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, with S-Bahn and regional trains, and attributes causes from IRIS codes into families **works, weather, technical, knock_on, staff, external**, with an explicit "unattributed" floor (only ~30 % of stops carry a cause). Seed journey stays regional inside a covered region: **leg 1 = the user's sample (RB 16, Nürnberg Hbf 04:34 → München Hbf 07:25), leg 2 = S 8 München Hbf 07:41 → München Flughafen Terminal 08:22, 16 min transfer.** One fixture per layer, swappable in minutes. - The app appears in the Android share sheet only when the PWA is **installed** from an **HTTPS** origin in Chrome and its manifest declares `share_target`. So the demo phone must install it via the tunnel URL first. iOS Safari does not support `share_target` (paste/drop path covers iPhone).

# error404.ai — PWA with 3D globe, DB-app share target, forecast, re-route and causes

## Context

We are building the user-facing product: an installable PWA where a traveller either **drops / pastes a DB connection** or **presses Share in the DB app, sees our app in the share sheet, taps it, and lands in our app** with the journey loaded. The app shows the route on a real 3D globe that zooms from Earth to the trains, the **probability each train is delayed and the plan fails**, **recommendations** (how early to leave home, what to do when a connection is missed, best re-route), and **causes of delay** with the evidence and the limitations. The team also presents by using this same app live on a big screen (large-type stage layout + keys that advance the real flow). Everything the user or audience sees is on the frontend; the backend only serves data.

Repo state (after `git pull`, main current): `app/frontend` is an empty placeholder, `app/backend` only has Nebius training routes, the model has no serving path. We code against the draft contract (`team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md`) and mock what is missing, with additive fields only.

Decisions already made with the user:
- **Map**: MapLibre GL JS `projection: 'globe'`, free Carto dark raster tiles (no key); service worker caches tiles seen in rehearsal.
- **Higgsfield**: assets only, ≤ 20 credits (icon, maskable icon, one backdrop). Website builder not used.
- **Share text** (real DB Navigator sample from the user, English, int.bahn.de):
  ```
  Nürnberg Hbf → München Hbf
  Sun 13.09.2026
  RB16 (59143)
  To München Hbf
  From 04:34 Nürnberg Hbf, Platform 5 C-F
  To 07:25 München Hbf, Platform 21
  View journey: https://int.bahn.de/en/buchung/start?vbid=e6285f4d-...
  ```
- **Data / route**: branch `origin/feat/db-route-multiscale` (matches the `error404-db-route` bucket) sources `piebro/deutsche-bahn-data` (CC BY 4.0, DB Timetables/IRIS data) for six commuter regions, Munich, Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, with S-Bahn and regional trains, and attributes causes from IRIS codes into families **works, weather, technical, knock_on, staff, external**, with an explicit "unattributed" floor (only ~30 % of stops carry a cause). Seed journey stays regional inside a covered region: **leg 1 = the user's sample (RB 16, Nürnberg Hbf 04:34 → München Hbf 07:25), leg 2 = S 8 München Hbf 07:41 → München Flughafen Terminal 08:22, 16 min transfer.** One fixture per layer, swappable in minutes. (S3 keys are not in `.env`, so the bucket objects were not listed.)

### Share-sheet facts the demo depends on
- The app appears in the Android share sheet only when the PWA is **installed** from an **HTTPS** origin in Chrome and its manifest declares `share_target`. So the demo phone must install it via the tunnel URL first. iOS Safari does not support `share_target` (paste/drop path covers iPhone).
- The DB app shares plain text (+ URL), so `share_target` uses `method: GET`, `action: /share`, params `title/text/url`. Our `/share` route reads the query, strips it from the URL, and runs parse → predict → recommend automatically.
- Same origin is required for the manifest, service worker and share target, so the backend serves the built frontend.

## Architecture

```
DB app Share ─▶ share sheet ─▶ error404 (installed PWA) ─▶ GET /share?text=…
Paste / drop text or .txt ─▶ Start screen                         │
                                                                   ▼
                    PWA (Vite + React 19, app/frontend/dist) ── same origin ──▶ Node backend :8000 (zero deps)
  POST /api/journeys/parse   share-parser       grammar for share text + stations table
  POST /api/predict          delay-prediction   mock prior now / PREDICT_URL → Python later; JS port of connection.py
  POST /api/recommend        recommendation     leave-home time, buffer, alternative
  POST /api/reroute          recommendation     next connections after a missed transfer (fixture, live Timetables if creds)
  GET  /api/causes           causes             cause-family shares per station / region (fixture from the pipeline output)
  GET  /api/seed/demo        pwa-shell          seed journey (also bundled in the frontend for offline)
Phone: cloudflared quick tunnel → https://…trycloudflare.com → localhost:8000
```

## The app, screen by screen (all frontend)

Full-bleed dark globe; a glass panel overlays it (right rail ≥ 1024 px, bottom sheet on phones). Bottom tab bar: **Plan · Forecast · Advice · Causes · Evidence**.

1. **Start / Plan** — globe turning over Europe. "Will my plan hold?" with: *Paste or drop* (textarea that also accepts drag-and-drop of text or a `.txt`), *Build* (from → to station search, time, add legs), *Demo journey*. A one-line hint "or press Share in the DB app and pick error404". Arriving from the share sheet skips this screen.
2. **Journey** — camera flies from space to the route; legs draw one by one with pins; one card per leg (train, from → to, planned times, transfer pill). Tap card ⇄ fly to leg; tap pin ⇄ highlight card. Globe stays draggable.
3. **Forecast** (visual 1) — per leg: **delay-probability bar chart** (P(delay ≤ 5), 5–15, 15–30, > 30, cancelled) from the returned distribution, "+8 min · likely 1–27", risk colour on the map leg; chain strip with transfers shrinking; fly-to on the breaking transfer; headline counts up to **"Probability your plan fails: NN%"**. Every number has "Why?" (reasoning, sources, confidence). **Buffer slider** re-chains live in the browser.
4. **Advice** (visuals 2 + 3) — verdict + weather-style advice. **"Leave home by HH:MM"**: user sets minutes from door to first station and an acceptable risk; the app picks the earliest departure (alternatives from the backend) that meets it and shows the time. **"I missed my connection"** per transfer → re-route list: next trains from that station with their own fail probability, best one highlighted and drawn dashed on the map; "Compare" toggles original vs re-route.
5. **Causes** (visual 4) — for the selected station or leg: stacked bar of cause-family shares (works, weather, technical, knock-on, staff, external, unattributed), a 7-day sparkline of station delay, and the IRIS text of the top cause. Data from `/api/causes` with a bundled fixture fallback; the source line states the dataset and the ~30 % attribution rate.
6. **Evidence** — three cards: *Data* (where it comes from: piebro/deutsche-bahn-data over DB IRIS, six regions, months covered, the DB Timetables API for live station lookup), *Results* (our model vs GPT/Claude baseline: one SVG bar chart from `public/proof.json` with the metric name, split, n; PNG fallback), *Limitations* (only 30 % of delays carry a cause; transfers treated as independent; regional trains in six regions, long-distance and other regions are out of scope; confidence is advisory, not calibrated; live prediction currently uses a prior when the model server is offline, shown as a badge). This card set is what the audience sees when the presenter explains evidence and limits.

**Stage mode** (`?stage=1` or key `S`): same screens, bigger type, progress dots; → / ← walk: Plan → share arrives → Journey → Forecast → Advice → re-route → Causes → Evidence. The team also presents by using this same app live on a big screen (large-type stage layout + keys that advance the real flow). Everything the user or audience sees is on the frontend; the backend only serves data.

content.content:
"""From per-train delay distributions to the chance that a change, and a journey, works out.

Transfer times are applied here, after the model. A change works when both trains run
and the planned buffer plus the connecting train's departure delay covers the arriving
train's delay plus the minimum transfer time. Trains are treated as independent, which
is optimistic when one disruption hits both; DB holding a connecting train is not modelled.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

import numpy as np


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TrainForecast:
    """A train's delay at one stop: P(delay = k minutes | runs) for k = 0.., and P(cancelled)."""

    probs: np.ndarray
    p_cancel: float = 0.0

    def normalised(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """The delay distribution scaled to sum to one."""
        total = float(np.sum(self.probs))
        if total <= 0:
            raise ValueError("delay distribution has no mass")
        return np.asarray(self.probs, dtype=np.float64) / total


def change_probability(arriving: TrainForecast, departing: TrainForecast, planned_buffer: float,
                       min_transfer: float) -> float:
    """P(both trains run and arrival delay - departure delay <= planned buffer - minimum transfer).

    Args:
        arriving: The incoming train's arrival delay at the change station.
        departing: The connecting train's departure delay at the change station.
        planned_buffer: Minutes between planned arrival and planned departure.
        min_transfer: Minutes needed to change, e.g. from RIS::Stations connecting times.
    """
    a, d = arriving.normalised(), departing.normalised()
    # Distribution of (arrival delay - departure delay): convolve with the reversed departure pmf.
    diff = np.convolve(a, d[::-1])
    offsets = np.arange(diff.size) - (d.size - 1)
    slack = np.floor(planned_buffer - min_transfer)
    p_made = float(diff[offsets <= slack].sum())
    return (1 - arriving.p_cancel) * (1 - departing.p_cancel) * p_made


def journey_probability(changes: list[tuple[TrainForecast, TrainForecast, float, float]],
                        final_arrival: TrainForecast | None = None, arrival_slack: float | None = None) -> dict:
    """Chain the changes of a journey into one success probability.

    Each change is ``(arriving, departing, planned_buffer, min_transfer)``. Changes are
    multiplied as if independent. A connecting train's departure delay and its later
    arrival delay are correlated, so this is an approximation that ignores that link.

    Args:
        changes: The journey's changes in order.
        final_arrival: The last train's arrival delay at the destination, if a deadline matters.
        arrival_slack: Minutes of lateness at the destination the traveller can absorb.

    Returns:
        Per-change probabilities and the probability that the whole plan works.
    """
    per_change = [change_probability(*change) for change in changes]
    success = float(np.prod(per_change)) if per_change else 1.0
    if final_arrival is not None and arrival_slack is not None:
        pmf = final_arrival.normalised()
        on_time = float(pmf[: int(np.floor(arrival_slack)) + 1].sum())
        success *= (1 - final_arrival.p_cancel) * on_time
    return {"change_probabilities": per_change, "plan_success": success, "plan_fail": 1 - success}


def point(minutes: int, size: int = 1000, p_cancel: float = 0.0) -> TrainForecast:
    """A forecast certain of one delay, handy for tests and fixed timetables."""
    probs = np.zeros(size)
    probs[minutes] = 1.0
    return TrainForecast(probs, p_cancel)

- higgsfield-brandkit: Create and extend complete visual brand systems through the Higgsfield CLI and bundled deterministic local tooling: palettes, SVG logo marks, typography, mockups, social graphics, packaging, signage, merchandise, posters, presentation decks, and editable PPTX/PDF brandbooks. Preserves official supplied assets, persists approvals locally, and regenerates only dependent outputs. Use when: "create a brand kit", "make a visual identity", "design a logo and brandbook", "apply this logo to branded assets", "make packaging or signage", or "extend our existing branding". Chain with higgsfield-generate for general image production and Marketing Studio brand-kits when importing website metadata for ads. NOT for unbranded image generation (use higgsfield-generate), product catalog photography (use higgsfield-product-photoshoot), website implementation (use higgsfield-websites), or native Figma/Canva/PSD/AI delivery.
- higgsfield-generate: Generate images/videos/3D assets/audio via Higgsfield AI. Defaults:
GPT Image 2.5 for image/design/text, Seedance 2.5 for
video, Nano Banana 2/Lite/Pro for character/reference
images, Marketing Studio for ads, Seed Audio 1.0 for audio.
Use when: "generate an image", "make a video", "animate
this photo", "image-to-video", "edit/stylize/remix this
image", "reframe this video", "edit this video from a
sketch", "create a 3D model/GLB", "create a sound effect",
"make music", "text-to-audio", "create an ad", "make a UGC
video", "unboxing", "presenter video", "import product from
URL", or "analyze video virality". Supports generic generation,
workflows, Marketing Studio, and Virality Predictor.
Chain with higgsfield-soul-id for face/identity consistency.
NOT for: Soul training, brand systems/brandbooks (use
higgsfield-brandkit), photoshoots, cards, YouTube thumbnails
(use higgsfield-youtube-thumbnail), explainers (use
higgsfield-video-explainer), playable games/assets (use
higgsfield-game-generation), or TTS.
- higgsfield-marketplace-cards: Generate marketplace product image cards through Higgsfield: compliant
main image, secondary product images, and A+ style content modules. Use when
the user asks for marketplace listing images, product detail cards,
secondary product images, product infographics, lifestyle listing shots,
A+ style content, marketplace image sets, or sales-ready product visuals.
Backend owns marketplace compliance references and prompt templates; this skill
only routes user intent to the CLI.
NOT for generic brand product photography without marketplace/listing context
(use higgsfield-product-photoshoot), video generation or UGC ads (use
higgsfield-generate), or Soul Character training (use higgsfield-soul-id).
- higgsfield-product-photoshoot: Generate brand-quality product images through Higgsfield product-photoshoot
prompt enhancement on GPT Image 2 / gpt_image_2. Entry point for professional
brand/product visuals.
Use when: "product photo", "studio shot", "lifestyle image", "Pinterest pin",
"hero/banner", "carousel", "ad creative", "Meta ads", "virtual try-on",
"model wearing", "person holding product", "closeup with hands",
"levitating/floating/splash product", "CGI/surreal product", "restyle",
"seasonal/aesthetic variation", or any product, brand, or paid-social creative.
Modes: product_shot, lifestyle_scene, closeup_product_with_person,
moodboard_pin, hero_banner, social_carousel, ad_creative_pack,
virtual_model_tryout, conceptual_product, restyle. Backend assembles the final
prompt; never freehand it.
NOT for: no-product text-to-image (use higgsfield-generate), branded avatar
video (use higgsfield-generate Marketing Studio), marketplace listing cards
(use higgsfield-marketplace-cards), Soul Character training (use
higgsfield-soul-id).
- higgsfield-soul-id: Train a Soul Character — a personalized model on a person's face that
Higgsfield uses for identity-faithful image and video generation.
Use when: "create my Soul", "train my face", "make my digital twin",
"build me an avatar", "learn my appearance", "create a character of me",
"set up identity for video", "I want my face in generated images".
Chain: train Soul (one-time, returns reference_id) → use in
higgsfield-generate via `--soul-id <id>` with models like
`text2image_soul_v2` or `soul_cinema_studio`.
NOT for: one-shot face swaps (use higgsfield-generate with --image),
named-character / non-photo avatars (use higgsfield-generate with prompt).
- higgsfield-video-explainer: Build a complete non-photoreal narrated explainer or story video from
ordered 10-second blocks: one narrator, one universal style key, one Seed
Audio take and one Gemini Omni clip per block, then server-side assembly
with explainer_video. Use when: "make an explainer video", "explain this in
a video", "turn this topic or document into a narrated video", "tell this
story as an animated video", "make a faceless narrated video", or "show me
explainer styles". Supports live CMS presets, custom style references,
mascot/faceless modes, two aspects, and optional burned subtitles. NOT for:
